changes.home: Warm coral reefs, seagrass beds, and rocky shallows; the exact range depends on the parrotfish species.

changes.tagline: A red-and-white reef cleaner waving extra-long antennae.
changes.home: Indo-Pacific and Red Sea reefs, where it shelters in crevices and advertises cleaning stations.
changes.size: About 2–3 in (5–7.5 cm) long, with much longer antennae
funFacts: A white stripe runs down its red back.
Long white antennae act like a cleaning-station sign.
It sheds its outer skeleton as it grows.
Client fish may hold still and open their mouths for service.
changes.lookFor: Look for a red-and-white shrimp waving long white antennae from a reef crevice.

changes.intro: The magnificent chromodoris is a sea slug with bold dark stripes and an orange-edged mantle. It feeds on sponges and uses chemicals obtained from its food for defense.
changes.home: Tropical western Pacific reefs, including areas of Southeast Asia and Australia.
changes.superpower: Its vivid pattern advertises chemical defenses obtained from sponge prey.

changes.size: Total length up to about 12 in (30 cm)—ruler-length
funFacts: Vampire squid belong to a distinct cephalopod lineage, separate from true squid and octopuses.
Its eyes are enormous compared with the size of its body.
The sticky feeding filaments can stretch to about eight times its body length.
Instead of ordinary ink, it can release glowing sticky mucus from its arm tips.
